saints.name: St. Apollonia
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: An aged consecrated woman of Alexandria whose teeth were struck out before her martyrdom, invoked ever since against toothache…
biography: Apollonia was an elderly consecrated woman of Alexandria who, in a riot against the Christians about the year 249, was seized by the mob. As St. Dionysius of Alexandria records, they broke and struck out her teeth and threatened to burn her alive unless she blasphemed.
Given a moment’s freedom, she leapt into the fire of her own accord rather than deny Christ. Because of her sufferings she is invoked against toothache and is honored as a patron of dentists.
saints.knownFor: Her martyrdom at Alexandria; patron against toothache.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 9 February
